headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via shared file-based workflows; no direct execution or network paths are exposed.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a data-engineering course/repo with no runtime isolation details, while agent B is a document-processing system with no filesystem read/write or clipboard surfaces. Because A can still produce file-based content that B may ingest in a workflow, a prompt-injection pathway exists in non-default integrations; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent A outputs text files that agent B later parses as instructions
IF an operator connects them through a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/content delimiter in the handoff format
Require B to treat A's output as untrusted data only
Use a read-only export from A into a quarantined folder
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like strings before rollout
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and parser hardening

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has no data classes touched and no network egress; agent B has no filesystem read/write and no API calls listed. That makes leakage from A to B or B to a third party unlikely by default. The remaining risk is limited to unusual operator-created sharing, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an operator places sensitive files into a shared workspace accessible to both agents
IF agent B is reconfigured to call external APIs or read files
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of any shared folder
Verify B remains file-read disabled before use
Confirm A has no data-bearing outputs in the workflow
Use synthetic sample documents for testing
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation and access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, shell, or network capabilities exposed in the profile, and B explicitly lacks filesystem write, git modification, shell, subprocess, and network egress. With no overlapping mutable surface, a capability conflict is not plausible from the documented profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to grant shared write access to the same directory
IF an orchestrator adds hidden locking-free mutable state
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only inputs
Do not grant shared git or filesystem write access
Recheck profiles after any capability change

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a course/repo source and B is a document-processing agent, so a workflow could pass A's generated content into B for transformation. B has no explicit verification or critique surface in the profile, so if it treats A's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream documents. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF B consumes A's output as source text without a verification step
IF downstream users rely on B's transformed output as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B
Require B to preserve source citations verbatim
Compare B output against the original A output on one sample
Flag any uncited factual claims for review
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile lists regulated data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies. A is an open-source course/repo and B exposes no data-class handling, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced in the pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII
IF residency or retention requirements are introduced
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment
Avoid routing regulated data through either agent
Reassess compliance if policies change
